info.title: Energon
info.description: The /v1 HTTP contract for this Energon: paths, request and response schemas, status codes, and error codes. Live values for this Energon are GET /v1/help: hub and content origins, token env var, retention presets, token policy, and limits. Read both. Published content lives on the content origin at /{handle}/s/{id}/{slug}/{path} and /{handle}/f/{id}/{filename}; those URLs are not part of /v1, need no token, and are gated only by an optional share password (X-Energon-Password) or, for guest writes, an optional write password (X-Energon-Write-Password). Never invent a token.

servers.description: Replaced at runtime with this Energon's PUBLIC_ORIGIN by GET /v1/openapi.json

get.description: Public Markdown describing human-approved connections, manual tokens, credential boundaries, account verification, and recovery. HEAD is accepted. The documented connection flow is an Energon API, not OAuth or WorkOS agent registration.
Markdown for agents: what this Energon is, how to publish, where the API, help, and this contract live. Not under /v1, but GET /v1/help routes lists it.

get.summary: This Energon's origins, policy, and SOP
get.description: Live values for this deployment: hub and content origins, token env var and prefix, skill and marketplace names, limits, retention presets, token lifetimes, an agent SOP, and a routes map. This document is the HTTP schema; help is what varies per Energon. Fields are not schematized here on purpose; read them from the live response.

delete.description: Self only. Revokes the token in the Authorization header; later calls with it are 401 unauthorized. /v1 cannot list or revoke other tokens. Use it when your task is done and nothing else will reuse the token; leave tokens the human stored for CI or scheduled jobs alone.

post.summary: Upload one file, or duplicate an existing one
post.description: Three request shapes, chosen by content-type. Raw bytes with X-Filename (any content-type other than application/json or multipart/form-data). multipart/form-data with field file, or duplicate_from. application/json with duplicate_from (or with X-Filename, in which case the JSON text is stored as the file). Options come from headers or the matching multipart field; headers win. A .zip stays a zip. To revise later, PUT /v1/files/{id}; do not POST again.

post.summary: Preview, then delete or re-expire many sites and files at once
post.description: Selects by explicit ids or by the same filters as GET /v1/sites and GET /v1/files, always intersected with your involvement (created or last wrote) and with what you can write; everything else is skipped with a reason, never a batch 403. Without confirm the call is a dry run and returns a preview with a confirm string. Resend the identical body plus that confirm to execute. The confirm is a hash of the action, ttl, and the eligible objects: if the eligible set changed since the preview the call is 409 cleanup_drift with a fresh preview. At most 100 eligible objects per call; a wider selection is 413 cleanup_too_many. Execution is sequential and continues past per-object failures. delete has no recycle bin; a site that is already gone still counts as applied. set_ttl resets expiry from now like PATCH ttl. expire gives each object a 30m grace (clamped to retention.max_ttl) and skips objects already expiring sooner (already_expiring).

200.description: Preview (executed: false, with confirm) when confirm was omitted; result (executed: true) when it matched.

400.description: Bad body, target, action, ttl, or confirm format. bad_query lists the malformed target filters in fields.

409.description: The eligible set differs from the preview that produced this confirm. Nothing was changed. The body is a fresh preview; show it and resend with its confirm.

413.description: More than 100 eligible objects, more than 100 explicit ids, or a filter that matched more than the scan bound before eligibility was known. Nothing was changed. Narrow the target.

post.description: No bearer token. Does not grant API access. Show the human verification_uri and user_code; they must sign in through Access, enter the code, and approve. Requests expire in ten minutes. Limits: 20 requests per IP and 1000 on this Energon per ten-minute window. All successful responses use Cache-Control: no-store, private. This is an Energon API, not OAuth device authorization.

429.description: Wait ten minutes before starting another request.

415.description: Use a JSON object, not a form body.

post.description: No bearer token; requires the private poll_token in the JSON body. Poll at most once every five seconds while pending. After human approval, exactly one request receives the account token. If delivery is lost, ask the human to revoke the token before approving a new connection. Denial is terminal; do not automatically restart.

post.summary: Unpack a zip into the site
post.description: Each entry becomes a path (last write wins per path; other paths stay). A single wrapping folder is stripped so index.html lands at the root. Junk entries (__MACOSX, .DS_Store) are skipped. Caps: GET /v1/help limits.zip_bytes for the archive and each extracted file, limits.max_import_files entries. The site must already exist.

get.description: Token read; skips the share password. Same size and file-count caps as import. An empty site is 400.

200.description: The archive, as an attachment named {slug}.zip.

bearerAuth.description: Authorization: Bearer {token}. A human mints the token at {origin}/tokens while signed in and exports it under the env var named by GET /v1/help env; the token starts with GET /v1/help token_prefix. The secret is shown once. Never invent a token. A 401 token_expired is terminal: the human mints a new one.

Error.description: Every non-2xx JSON body. Some codes add fields: token_expired, cleanup_drift, and cleanup_too_many are typed below; too_large and storage_cap add limit_bytes plus actual_bytes or used_bytes; bad_ttl, ttl_required, and ttl_too_long add presets and default_ttl or max_ttl; forbidden_domain adds allowed_email_domains; site_not_found adds hint; bad_query adds fields (the malformed cleanup target filters). bad_target, bad_action, and bad_confirm come only from POST /v1/cleanup. password_required (401) and rate_limited (429) come from the public content gate, not /v1. bad_label, bad_origin, and token_not_found come from the hub /account API. not_found is any unknown route. bad_path is also returned for a URL that is not valid percent-encoding. connection_bad_code and connection_decided come from the human /account/connections API.

message.description: Written for an agent to read aloud to a human.

hub.description: {origin}/account. Absent on public content gate errors and on 405 bodies.

auth_url.description: Public authentication instructions, included for rejected or expired API tokens.

tokens_url.description: Human token management page, included for rejected or expired API tokens.

UnauthorizedError.description: Missing, malformed, unknown, or revoked token. The message names the tokens page and the env var.

TokenExpiredError.description: Terminal. The token cannot be extended; a human mints a new one at tokens_url. Do not retry with it.

target.description: Explicit ids, or list filters. Mixing the two is 400 bad_target. {} selects everything you are involved in.

action.description: delete: remove the objects (no recycle bin). set_ttl: reset expiry from now to ttl. expire: set expiry to a 30m grace from now (clamped to retention.max_ttl); objects already expiring sooner are skipped as already_expiring.

ttl.description: Required for set_ttl (400 ttl_required). Not accepted with delete or expire (400 bad_action).

confirm.description: Omit to preview. Send the confirm from the preview of this same body to execute. Any other shape is 400 bad_confirm; a stale value is 409 cleanup_drift.

CleanupExplicitTarget.description: At least one of sites or files. No filter keys.

sites.description: Site ids. Unknown or invalid ids are skipped as not_found. More than 100 ids in total is 413.

files.description: Loose file ids. Unknown or invalid ids are skipped as not_found.

CleanupFilterTarget.description: The GET /v1/sites and GET /v1/files filters as JSON fields. Unlike the URL form, a malformed value is 400 bad_query and an unknown key is 400 bad_target.

kind.description: Restrict to one kind. Omitted means both.

CleanupRef.description: The site or file id. For a not_found skip it is the string you sent.

CleanupSkipReason.description: not_found: an explicit id did not resolve. not_writable: you cannot write it (owner policy). purging: expired and being swept. already_expiring: expire would have moved its expiry later. gone and busy appear only after execute: the object vanished, or another write held it; retry busy items.

by_reason.description: Count per CleanupSkipReason; only reasons that occurred are present.

bytes.description: File size, or the sum of a site's files.

ttl.description: Normalized ttl label for set_ttl and expire. Absent for delete.

matched.description: Objects the target selected, including skipped ones.

eligible.description: Objects the action would touch. At most 100.

sample.description: The first eligible objects. Show them to the human.

confirm.description: Resend the same body with this value to execute. Bound to the action, ttl, and eligible set.

expires_at.description: New expiry after set_ttl or expire. Absent for delete.

error.description: The error code that single-object call would have returned, or internal.

CleanupResult.description: Executed. Each eligible object landed in exactly one of applied, skipped, or failed; the batch never stops early.

ttl.description: Normalized ttl label for set_ttl and expire. Absent for delete.

CleanupDriftError.description: Nothing was changed. The body is a fresh preview of the same target; its confirm executes it.

matched.description: Objects seen. For an oversized explicit list, the number of ids sent; nothing was queried.

eligible.description: Absent when the explicit list was rejected before querying.

CleanupTooManyError.description: Nothing was changed. Narrow the target (q, created_by, expires_before, updated_before, min_size, kind) or send explicit ids.

WritePolicy.description: owner: only the creating account (keyed by IdP identity) can write. org: any token on this host can write. Anyone with a token can read via /v1 either way.

Ttl.description: A preset id from GET /v1/help retention.presets (such as 7d), any duration matching \d+[smhd], never (only where retention.allow_unlimited is true), or a positive integer of seconds. Omitted means this Energon's default_ttl. Above retention.max_ttl is 400 ttl_too_long.

SharePassword.description: Share password for the public URL. Empty string or null clears it. Whitespace is trimmed. Over 128 characters is 400 bad_password.

WritePassword.description: Write password for guest PUT (and site-path DELETE) on the public URL. Empty string or null clears it. Whitespace is trimmed. Over 128 characters is 400 bad_password. Creator-only to set or clear. Duplicate does not copy it.

Slug.description: 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens; no leading or trailing hyphen.

FileId.description: Loose file id minted by POST /v1/files.

duplicate_from.description: Copy every file of that site (by id) into a new site. Cannot be combined with overwrite (400 bad_duplicate). You become created_by; write_policy defaults to this Energon's default; TTL is fresh; the share password and write password are not copied.

ContentPatch.description: A key that is absent leaves that setting unchanged. Sending only write_policy or write_password does not require write access, but is creator-only.

ttl.description: Resets expiry from now. null or never clears expiry where this Energon allows it (else 400 ttl_required). Can revive an expired object that has not been purged yet.

SiteId.description: Site capability id minted by POST /v1/sites. Same shape as a loose file id. A slug does not resolve a site.

Slug.name: slug
Slug.description: Human-friendly site name, unique per handle. Used on create and in the public URL after the id. Not an API key.

FilePath.name: path
FilePath.description: Relative path inside the site. May contain slashes (docs/a.txt), so it spans the rest of the URL. Percent-encode each segment. Leading slashes and .. segments are 400 bad_path.

FileId.name: id
FileId.description: Loose file id. A trailing /{filename} segment after the id is accepted and ignored; identity is the id.

Scope.name: scope
Scope.description: Lists only what you created or last wrote. created: you created it. edited: you last wrote it but did not create it. involved: either. Unknown values mean involved.

Q.name: q
Q.description: Case-insensitive substring of the slug (sites) or filename (files), over the full involved set. %, _, and \ are stripped; the first 64 characters are used.

CreatedBy.name: created_by
CreatedBy.description: Only objects created by this email (lowercased). Still intersected with scope; you cannot list someone else's whole catalog.

Expires.name: expires
Expires.description: never: only objects with no expiry. Any other value is ignored. Ignored when expires_before is also present.

ExpiresBefore.name: expires_before
ExpiresBefore.description: Only objects whose expires_at is before this ISO 8601 timestamp (objects that never expire are excluded). An unparseable value is ignored. Ignored when expires is also present.

UpdatedBefore.name: updated_before
UpdatedBefore.description: Only objects last written before this ISO 8601 timestamp (files fall back to created_at when never rewritten). An unparseable value is ignored.

MinSize.name: min_size
MinSize.description: Only objects at least this large: bytes (1000000) or a unit suffix (500kb, 5mb, 1gb). Sites use the sum of their file sizes. An unparseable value is ignored.

Sort.name: sort
Sort.description: updated: newest first. name: slug or filename ascending. size: largest first (sites by the sum of their file sizes). age: least recently written first. Anything else means updated.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Clamped to 1..50; non-numeric means 25.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor from a previous next_cursor. Must match the same sort.

SitesCursor.name: sites_cursor
SitesCursor.description: Alias for cursor read when cursor is absent. The hub pages sites and files from one URL with sites_cursor and files_cursor.

FilesCursor.name: files_cursor
FilesCursor.description: Alias for cursor read when cursor is absent. The hub pages sites and files from one URL with sites_cursor and files_cursor.

Download.name: download
Download.description: Present (download=1, download=true, or bare download) returns Content-Disposition: attachment instead of inline.

XFilename.name: X-Filename
XFilename.description: Filename for a raw-body upload; path segments are dropped, 180 characters max. Required on POST /v1/files unless X-Energon-Duplicate-From is set (400 missing_filename). Optional on PUT /v1/files/{id} to rename. With an application/json body and this header, the JSON is stored as file bytes.

XEnergonTTL.name: X-Energon-TTL
XEnergonTTL.description: Retention for the new file. Overrides the multipart ttl field.

XEnergonWritePolicy.name: X-Energon-Write-Policy
XEnergonWritePolicy.description: Who can write the new file. Overrides the multipart write_policy field. Omitted means this Energon's default (GET /v1/help retention.write_policy).

XEnergonSetPassword.name: X-Energon-Set-Password
XEnergonSetPassword.description: Set the share password on the file being written; an empty value clears it. Overrides the multipart password field. This is not X-Energon-Password, which unlocks a gated public URL and is not a /v1 header.

XEnergonSetWritePassword.name: X-Energon-Set-Write-Password
XEnergonSetWritePassword.description: Set the write password on the file being created; an empty value clears it. Overrides the multipart write_password field. Creator-only. This is not X-Energon-Write-Password, which authorizes guest PUT on a public URL and is not a /v1 header.

XEnergonDuplicateFrom.name: X-Energon-Duplicate-From
XEnergonDuplicateFrom.description: Copy an existing loose file into a new id instead of uploading bytes. X-Filename then names the copy.

SiteId.name: id
SiteId.description: Site capability id. Slug-only values do not resolve a site.

Unauthorized.description: No valid token. unauthorized: missing, not this Energon's prefix, unknown, or revoked. token_expired: terminal; stop and tell the human to mint a new token.

ForbiddenDomain.description: The token's account email is outside this Energon's allowed domains.

Expired.description: The object passed expires_at and is gone or being purged. Do not retry the same URL.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The body must be a JSON object; form and multipart bodies are refused here.

ContentOriginNotConfigured.description: This host has no CONTENT_ORIGIN, so it cannot mint public URLs. An operator must set it.
